Title: AKU to host infectious diseases symposium
NewsSummary: The Aga Khan University (AKU) will hold a two-day Symposium on Infectious Diseases on September 20 and September 21, 1999, which will be followed by a Molecular Biology Workshop on infectious disease from September 22-26.

content.text: The Aga Khan University (AKU) will hold a two-day Symposium on Infectious Diseases on September 20 and September 21, 1999, which will be followed by a Molecular Biology Workshop on infectious disease from September 22-26. The major focus of the symposium will be infectious diseases of national relevance, such as tuberculosis, hepatitis, malaria and typhoid. In 1990, the worldwide estimates of deaths over the age of five resulting from these diseases were: 1.9 million for tuberculosis, 0.3 million for malaria and 2 million for other tropical diseases. Pakistan is among the top ten countries for deaths from these diseases. Tuberculosis was among the two major causes of deaths in women in 1990. These figures have risen dramatically in the last decade.

The prevention and treatment of infectious diseases, therefore represent one of the greatest challenges of national health care in Pakistan. This forum is being organized to bring together international and national experts and researchers in key areas of infectious disease of national relevance. The main objective of the symposium is to stimulate further research in order to reduce mortality and morbidity from these diseases.

Scholars of international repute have been invited to give the keynote plenary talks. Dr Douglas Young of the Department of Microbiology, Imperial College School of Medicine, University of London, will speak on"Mycobacterial genomics and its applications to diagnosis and epidemiology," while Dr Andrew Lever of Cambridge University will discuss the "Gene therapy of persistent viral infections." Other speakers will discuss epidemiology, molecular biology, pathogenesis and management of infectious diseases.

There will be oral and poster presentations in sessions devoted to mycobacterial, bacterial, viral and parasitic diseases. A general session will cover aspects of medicine and health other than infectious disease. In addition to AKU faculty, participants will include faculty and researchers from national medical colleges and universities, representatives of the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Pakistan, general practitioners, and all those health professionals who have an interest in infectious disease and health related issues.
